data.headline: Fed Governor Christopher Waller now leans toward a conditional September hold, according to WSJ’s Nick Timiraos. If August inflation keeps moving toward 2%, he favors no change; a hot print could put a rate hike back in play.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller says the September rate decision will depend heavily on next week’s August CPI report. He called the recent improvement in three-month core inflation encouraging, while keeping a rate hike on the table.
FED WALLER: CURRENT FED RATES MAY BE ENOUGH TO BRING INFLATION BACK TO 2%—NO RUSH TO CUT UNTIL MORE PROGRESS EMERGES
